title: Swap Lab
description:
Prove how parameter passing works.
```
Before: a=1 b=2   (&a=0x7ffc10 &b=0x7ffc14)
swapByValue:     a=1 b=2   ✗ unchanged
swapByReference: a=2 b=1   ✓
swapByPointer:   a=1 b=2   ✓ (swapped back)
Inside swapByValue: &x=0x7ffbe0 (different address = a copy!)
```
hints: The by-value version swaps two *copies*; the address it prints is not `a`'s address, which is the proof. A reference parameter (`int& x`) is another name for the caller's variable, so swapping it swaps `a` and `b` (lesson 4.03).
With pointers, swap what they point at: `const int temp{ *x }; *x = *y; *y = temp;` and call it with `swapByPointer(&a, &b)`.
requirements: Print addresses inside and outside to *show* copying
A template `swapAny(T& a, T& b)` tested with `int`, `double`, `std::string`
